note: Kings Canyon National Park campground in the Grant Grove area, 4 miles from the Kings Canyon entrance on Highway 180, under open evergreen forest. Only about 20 of the sites take an RV or trailer; the rest are tent sites. Bear-box food storage is required. Arrive by Highway 180: the parks advise against vehicles over 22 ft on the Generals Highway between Potwisha and the Giant Forest Museum. --Claude
summary: Crystal Springs (Kings Canyon NP, federal:nps): rec.gov facility/rules/rates/catalog/availability + nps.gov campgrounds page (headless) + Esri. Ownership NPS confirmed. $32, reservation only with a 2-day booking window (overrides the inherited 180), 14-night max, season 05-20 to 09-14 (2026). 35 sites, ~20 fit a 23-ft rig, max 41 ft. Not waterfront kept. Phone, website and pin unchanged.
flags: BOOKING WINDOW: window_opens_days 2 overrides the inherited federal 180 (rec.gov reservationWindow 2 Days; nps.gov 'Reservations can be made up to two days in advance. All sites are reservation only.'), so fcfs is 'never'.

ACCESS (no drop): rec.gov advises 'Vehicles over 22 feet are not advised between Potwisha Campground and the Giant Forest Museum ... Vehicles over 22 feet should use the Kings Canyon National Park Entrance.' The campground is reached from the Kings Canyon (Hwy 180) entrance without using that stretch, so this is a routing caveat, now in the note, not a restriction on the campground.

FIT: of 34 catalog sites, 21 permit an RV or trailer and 19-21 fit a 23-ft rig (one site lists RV/Trailer with length 0, one lists a trailer with length 0); 13 are tent only. sites.count kept at the agency's 35.
STATUS: nps.gov shows CLOSED for the season (normal; it opens late May).
Phone 559-565-4357 matches rec.gov's 'facility specific information' line (the facility_phone field shows 559 565 3341). Website unchanged.

The previous summary's guess that this could be the Forest Service's Crystal Springs on SR 88 (Alpine County) is ruled out: the stored pin, the rec.gov id and the note are all the Kings Canyon campground, and federal:nps is correct.
